title: First, Next, Last
objectives: I can use first, next, then, and finally to tell steps in order.
I can use before and after to tell what happens earlier or later.
I can retell a short story or routine in the right order.
I can explain how to do something with order words.
rationale: Order words let first graders retell a story, explain a routine, and follow directions. The four order adverbs (first, next, then, finally) come before the two time words (before, after) because children can hear a sequence long before they can say which event came earlier. This unit also revisits explain and remember from unit 1, since children explain a sequence with these words and remember it by saying the order out loud.

words.def: Coming at the very start, before the others.
words.nonExample: The last step in a recipe does not come first.

apps.writing: Start your writing with first to show the first step.

cloze.s: Mom said, "___, put on your socks. Then put on your shoes."

cloze2.s: Ben ate his soup ___ and saved the cookie for last.

misuse.s: I put on my shoes first, after I finished walking to school.
misuse.why: First means before anything else. You cannot put on shoes after you have already walked.

visual.alt: Three steps in a row with the first step marked number one.

words.ex: Next, we put the lid on the box.
words.ex2: Mom stirred the soup, and next she added salt.
words.nonExample: What you did an hour ago is not what comes next.

apps.academic: Next, write your name on your paper.
apps.writing: Use next to show the step that comes after the first one.

cloze.s: We washed the dishes. ___, we dried them with a towel.

cloze2.s: Add the flour. ___ pour in the milk and stir.

misuse.s: Ben ate lunch, and next he ate breakfast.
misuse.why: Breakfast comes before lunch. Next means what comes after, so this does not fit.

visual.alt: An arrow pointing from one step to the step right after it.

words.def: After that; at a time that comes later.
words.ex: Mix the paint, then put some on the paper.
words.ex2: We played outside, and then we went home.

apps.writing: Use then to join two steps in a row.

cloze.s: Mia put on her coat, ___ she walked out into the snow.

cloze2.s: First Jo ran to the door. ___ she opened it and went in.

misuse.s: I ate my snack, then I opened the bag it was in.
misuse.why: You open the bag before you eat the snack, so then does not fit.

visual.alt: A first step, an arrow, and a second step that comes after.

words.def: At the end, or after a long time.
words.ex: Finally, the bus came, and we all cheered.
words.ex2: After many tries, Ben finally tied his shoes.
words.nonExample: The beginning of a story is not where finally comes.

apps.writing: Use finally to show the last step.

cloze.s: We waited and waited for the rain to stop. ___, the sun came out.

cloze2.s: The snow was deep, but we ___ got to the top of the hill.

misuse.s: Finally, our trip is just beginning, and we have not left the house yet.
misuse.why: Finally means at the end or after a long wait. This is the very start.

visual.alt: A line of steps with the last step marked at the end.

words.def: Earlier than the time something else happens.
words.ex: Wash your hands before you eat lunch.
words.ex2: The bell rang before the class finished the song.
words.nonExample: You do not put on your shoes before your socks.

apps.academic: Read the question before you answer.
apps.spoken: I get my bag before I go.
apps.writing: Use before to tell which thing happens earlier.

cloze.s: Put on your boots ___ you go out in the snow.

cloze2.s: Ruth brushes her teeth ___ she goes to bed, so they are clean at night.

misuse.s: We eat lunch before we cook it.
misuse.why: Before means earlier. You cook food first and eat it after.

visual.alt: Two boxes in a row with the earlier one on the left.

words.def: Later than the time something else happens.
words.ex2: The flowers grew tall after the rain fell on them.
words.nonExample: You do not eat dinner after you go to sleep.

apps.academic: Line up after the bell rings.
apps.writing: Use after to tell which thing happens later.

cloze.s: Ben took a nap ___ lunch, because he was sleepy and full.

cloze2.s: First the clouds came, and the flowers grew tall ___ the rain fell on them.

misuse.s: I eat the apple, and after I finish, I take the first bite.
misuse.why: After means later. The first bite comes before you finish eating.

visual.alt: Two boxes in a row with the later one on the right.

passage.title: Making a Sandwich
paras: Ben helps Dad make a sandwich. First, they get two slices of bread. Next, Ben spreads on the jam. Then Dad adds peanut butter. Finally, they put the slices together. They wash their hands before they start and after they eat the tasty sandwich.

qs.q: What do Ben and Dad do first?
qs.why: The story says First, they get two slices of bread.

qs.q: What comes right after Ben spreads on the jam?
qs.why: The word Then shows that Dad adds peanut butter right after Ben spreads the jam.

qs.q: What does the word finally tell us about putting the slices together?
choices: It is a step they skip.
qs.why: Finally means at the end, so putting the slices together comes last.

write.prompt: Draw three steps for something you do every day. Tell about them with first, next, and finally.
write.frame: First I ___. Next I ___. Finally I ___.

study.task: Draw three boxes in a row. Write first, next, and finally above them. Draw and tell about your morning.

groups.label: words that tell what is earlier or later

sentences: Tell how you get ready for school. Use first and then.
Say a sentence about your day with the word before.
Write a sentence about what you do after school.

combine.model: I put on my coat before I go outside.
We played outside after we ate lunch.

discuss: What do you do first when you wake up?
What is the last thing you do at night? Use finally.
produce.explain: Explain how to make your favorite snack. Use first, next, and finally.

constructed.prompt: Tell the steps for washing your hands. Use first, next, and finally.
look: steps are in a sensible order
each step is a complete idea
constructed.model: First, I turn on the water. Next, I rub soap on my hands. Finally, I dry them with a towel.

constructed.prompt: Say one thing you do before lunch and one thing you do after lunch.
look: the two things really happen in that order
constructed.model: I wash my hands before lunch. I play outside after lunch.

teacher.overview: Children learn four order words and two time words, then use them to retell a short routine and to explain their own steps. The unit revisits explain and remember from unit 1.

notes.va.first.adv: Act out a real routine such as lining up and have children say First plus the step. Many children say 'first' for any step, so ask 'What is the very start?'
notes.va.next.adv: Use a three-picture strip. Point to the step right after the first one and say Next plus the step. Next means right after, not later.
notes.va.then.adv: Then and next are close. Let children use either between middle steps; the goal is a clear order, not one right word.
notes.va.finally.adv: Finally marks the end or a long wait. Pair it with a picture of the last step, and ask 'What took a long time?' for the second sense.
notes.va.before.conj: Use two cards, shoes and socks. Ask which goes on earlier. Say the same fact two ways: 'Socks go on before shoes' and 'Shoes go on after socks.'
notes.va.after.conj: After is the mirror of before. Do both in one day: 'Before lunch we wash, after lunch we play' so children hear them as opposites.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: 'I want to tell how to plant a seed. First, I put soil in a cup. Next, I push the seed in. Then I add water. Finally, I put the cup in the sun. I wash my hands after I plant, and I remember to do it before I touch my lunch.'
discuss: Why does it help to tell steps in order?
What happens before school and what happens after school?
misconceptions: Before means later and after means earlier.
First and finally mean the same thing.
Then can only be used with next.
Order words have to be said in a loud voice to count.
extend: Children cut apart a four-picture story strip and put it in order, then retell it with order words.
Play 'Simon Sequence': give two moves with before or after and children do them in the right order.
teacher.reviewAdvice: Revisit the four order words the next day with a new routine, again at one week, and use them in every retell. They return when children tell cause and effect in unit 3.

frames: First, I ___. Next, I ___. Finally, I ___.
wida.oral: Partner A tells three steps for a routine using first, next, and finally. Partner B holds up fingers for each step and says what happens last.

needsReview: Spanish glosses (primero, luego, finalmente, antes de, después de) are not reviewed by a native speaker; luego for next and then needs a native check because entonces is also used for then.
First, next, then, and finally are taught as sequence adverbs; before and after are taught only as conjunctions (before/after a clause) to keep the sense simple.
